pages.text: "Bread!" Mumu the little brother stretched his neck toward the table and grabbed steaming bread in his beak. No chewing, just gulp! "Eat faster, eat more!" he said.
Big sister Dodo tore off little pieces and chewed. Mumu stuffed another lump into his bulging beak. "I'll eat all three!" The bread plate was already half empty.
Suddenly—"Hic! Hic!" His throat felt tight. He had gulped too fast. The hiccups wouldn't stop. Mumu rubbed his neck with both wings.

Dad from the mill stood behind him. One wing stroked his back; the other offered a water bowl. "Slowly. Swallow." When Mumu put his beak to the bowl, the hiccups stopped. "Shall we eat like grinding at the mill?" Mumu nodded.
Dad whispered, "There's a mill inside your beak too. Pound with your beak, and bread becomes soft." Mumu imagined a tiny waterwheel pounding bread. He called, "That's why we chew well!"
"Shall we play milling?" Dad put both wings on the table and bent low. "Small bites, chew well! Pound several times with your beak, then swallow!" Dodo grew excited too. "Let's see who chews best!"

Mumu tore bread into pieces on his plate, then chewed one well with his beak. One, two, three... The more he pounded, the more sweetness filled his beak. "It tasted this good?" Small bites, chew well!
The plate was empty. Mumu leaned back in his chair and spread both wings wide. "My tummy doesn't feel tight at all!" No hiccups either. One tail flick. He did it!
That evening, Mumu pounded small bread pieces with his beak. "One, small bites! Two, chew well several times with my beak! Three, when it's all pounded, swallow!" He called, "Small bites, chew well!"
Dad lifted Mumu into his arms. "Our Mumu, champion of the mill inside his beak!" Slow, thorough pounding tastes better and feels good in your tummy. Mumu called, "Small bites, chew well!"
